claim: The Legislature convenes at noon on the second Wednesday in January each year; a regular session ends on a day set by concurrent resolution
quote: The legislature shall meet at the seat of government on the second Wednesday in January of each year at twelve o'clock noon.

claim: A new law takes effect 90 days after the session ends unless two-thirds of each house give it immediate effect
quote: No act shall take effect until the expiration of 90 days from the end of the session at which it was passed

claim: Every election is held on a regular election date: the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May, August or November (plus the presidential primary date)
quote: The August regular election date, which is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in August.

claim: The primary for offices elected at the general election is held on the August regular election date
quote: the primary election shall be held on the August regular election date

claim: The general November election is the November regular election date in an even-numbered year
quote: "General election" or "general November election" means the election held on the November regular election date in an even numbered year.

claim: The odd year general election is the November regular election date in an odd-numbered year, and the odd year primary is the August date in an odd year
quote: "Odd year general election" means the election held on the November regular election date in an odd numbered year.

claim: Cities elect city officers at the odd year general election by default, but a city already on an annual or even-year November schedule keeps it
quote: A city that holds its regular election for a city office annually or in the even year on the November regular election date shall continue holding elections on that schedule.

claim: Odd-year city elections are the default rule
quote: A city shall hold its regular election for a city office at the odd year general election.

claim: A city on the May date holds no regular primary
quote: If a city's regular election is held on the May regular election date, the city shall not hold a regular primary election.

claim: A city council may move its regular election between the permitted schedules by resolution, including from odd years to even years
quote: may change its regular election schedule to the even year general election and the even year primary election by adopting a resolution in compliance with section 642

claim: Villages elect at the general (even-year November) election, run by the township clerk, with no primary
quote: A village shall hold its regular election for a village office at the general election and the appropriate township clerk shall conduct the election.

claim: Villages hold no regular primary
quote: A village shall not hold a regular primary election.

claim: School board members are elected at the general November election
quote: A school district shall hold its regular election for the office of school board member at the general November election.

claim: At least one school board member is elected at each regular school election; school district includes community college districts
quote: At least 1 school board member for a school district must be elected at each of the school district's regular elections held as provided in section 642c.

claim: School board candidates file nonpartisan nominating petitions
quote: except that the petition must be nonpartisan

claim: School board members serve 4- or 6-year terms set by the district's bylaws
quote: Members of the board of a general powers school district shall be elected by the school electors for terms of 4 or 6 years, as provided by the school district's bylaws.

claim: The candidates with the most votes, up to the number of seats, win school board races (plurality)
quote: That number of candidates equal to the number of individuals to be elected who receive the greatest number of votes cast at the election

claim: County clerk, treasurer, register of deeds, prosecutor, sheriff, drain commissioner and surveyor are elected every fourth year from the 2000 general election (presidential years), unless abolished or combined
quote: shall be elected at the 2000 general November election and every fourth year after that

claim: The constitution requires a four-year sheriff, clerk, treasurer, register of deeds and prosecuting attorney in every organized county
quote: There shall be elected for four-year terms in each organized county a sheriff, a county clerk, a county treasurer, a register of deeds and a prosecuting attorney

claim: County offices are nominated at a party primary held in August before the general November election
quote: A general primary election of all political parties shall be held in every county of this state on the Tuesday succeeding the first Monday in August

claim: The candidate with the most votes wins a county office (plurality, no runoff)
quote: received the greatest number of votes and shall declare such candidates to be duly elected

claim: County commissioners are elected in partisan elections
quote: Nominations and elections for commissioners must be by partisan elections.

claim: County commissioners elected at or after the 2024 general election serve four-year terms (previously two, with state representatives)
quote: The term of office of each commissioner elected at or after the 2024 general November election is 4 years.

claim: Each county is apportioned into 5 to 21 single-member commissioner districts
quote: apportion the county into not less than 5 nor more than 21 county commissioner districts

claim: Smaller counties have a lower cap on commissioners (not more than 7 under 5,001 people, up to 21 over 50,000)
quote: Number of county commissioners based on county population

claim: Commissioner districts are single-member districts
quote: All districts shall be single-member districts

claim: Older laws and the constitution say 'board of supervisors'; that now means the county board of commissioners
quote: shall be deemed to mean county commissioners and county boards of commissioners

claim: Any county may adopt a charter under general law
quote: Any county may frame, adopt, amend or repeal a county charter in a manner and with powers and limitations to be provided by general law

claim: A county charter must provide for partisan election of the board of commissioners from single-member districts
quote: The charter must also provide for the partisan election of members of the legislative body from single-member districts

claim: A county charter must keep the sheriff, prosecutor, clerk, treasurer and register of deeds elected on a partisan basis
quote: The partisan election of a sheriff, a prosecuting attorney, a county clerk, a county treasurer, and a register of deeds

claim: A charter county under 1.5 million people elects a county executive at large on a partisan basis
quote: for a salaried county executive, who is elected at large on a partisan basis

claim: The optional unified form comes with either an appointed county manager or an elected county executive
quote: An elected county executive, who shall comply with the qualifications and exercise the responsibilities detailed in sections 8, 9, 10, and 11.

claim: Under the optional unified form, a county executive is elected on a partisan basis for four years
quote: shall be elected on a partisan basis for a term of 4 years

claim: Detroit (the only city over 600,000) sits in a county organized under the 1966 charter county act, i.e. Wayne County is a charter county
quote: If a city with a population of more than 600,000 that is located in a county organized under 1966 PA 293

claim: Every organized township elects a supervisor, clerk, treasurer and up to four trustees
quote: a supervisor, a clerk, a treasurer, and not to exceed four trustees

claim: Township officers are elected at the even-year general November election, on the cycle that began in 1980 (presidential years)
quote: At the 1980 general November election, there shall be elected by ballot all of the following township officers

claim: Township officers serve four-year terms
quote: the term of office of all township officers listed in section 358 is 4 years

claim: A general law township has two trustees, or four if it reaches 5,000 people (or 3,000 voters) and its voters approve
quote: In other townships there shall be 2 trustees.

claim: Township candidates are nominated at a party primary in August
quote: the qualified and registered electors of each political party may vote for party candidates for township offices

claim: Township candidates appear under a party heading on the primary ballot
quote: To obtain the printing of the name of an individual as a candidate for nomination by a political party for a township office under the particular party heading

claim: A township of 2,000 or more people may incorporate as a charter township
quote: A township, having a population of 2,000 or more inhabitants according to the most recent regular or special federal or state census of the inhabitants of the township may incorporate as a charter township.

claim: A charter township has a seven-member board (supervisor, clerk, treasurer, four trustees) elected under the Michigan election law
quote: a township board of 7 members composed of the supervisor, the township clerk, the township treasurer, and 4 trustees

claim: In a charter township the supervisor presides and is the board's executive officer, with an equal vote
quote: the supervisor shall be the presiding and executive officer of the board and shall have an equal voice and vote in the proceedings of the board

claim: The voter marks one party's ticket only in a primary; a ballot with more than one party's ticket marked is void
quote: A ballot on which more than 1 party ticket has been voted is void.

claim: A primary voter chooses the party primary they want on the day
quote: Permit an elector in a primary election to vote for the candidates in the party primary of the elector's choice.

claim: Only the presidential primary requires a written party choice, which becomes a public record
quote: In order to vote at a presidential primary election, an elector shall indicate in writing

claim: A candidate without party affiliation files a qualifying petition, available for partisan offices
quote: A person may file a qualifying petition for a partisan office or office of justice of the supreme court.

claim: An independent cannot pay a filing fee instead of petitioning
quote: A filing fee shall not be tendered instead of a qualifying petition.

claim: A person who files a qualifying petition cannot also seek a party nomination for that election or any election that calendar year
quote: shall not file a partisan nominating petition or filing fee, and shall not be nominated as a candidate by write-in vote or by a political party convention, caucus, or committee

claim: Signers must be registered voters of the district, and may not sign more petitions for the same office than there are seats
quote: An individual shall not knowingly sign more petitions for the same office than there are persons to be elected to the office.

claim: A qualifying petition may not refer to a political party
quote: A qualifying petition for a candidate without party affiliation must not contain a reference to a political party.

claim: Qualifying petition signers must be registered electors of the district
quote: shall be signed by a number of qualified and registered electors of the district that is represented by the office being sought

claim: If no more than twice as many candidates file as there are seats, the nonpartisan odd-year primary is skipped, unless a city charter says otherwise
quote: not more than twice the number of candidates as there are persons to be elected to that office have filed, the primary for that office must not be held

claim: A city charter may elect a candidate outright at the primary on more than 50% of the vote
quote: If a charter provides for the election at the primary of a candidate who receives more than 50% of the votes cast for that office

claim: City officers' nomination, election and terms follow the city charter, subject to the Election Law's timing sections
quote: the qualifications, nomination, election, appointment, term of office, and removal from office of a city officer must be in accordance with the charter provisions governing the city

claim: A city may lie in more than one county
quote: the county in which the largest portion of the population of the city resides

claim: A home rule city charter chooses partisan, nonpartisan or preferential ballots, and may have the council pick the mayor
quote: Elections may be by a partisan, nonpartisan, or preferential ballot, or by any other legal method of voting.

claim: A home rule city charter may provide for the council to select the mayor
quote: The city charter may provide for the selection of the mayor by the legislative body.

claim: A home rule city charter elects a mayor and a legislative body; clerk, treasurer and assessor may be elected or appointed
quote: for the election or appointment of a clerk, a treasurer, an assessor or board of assessors

claim: A home rule city charter chooses partisan or nonpartisan primary, petition or convention for nominations
quote: The nomination of elective officers by partisan or nonpartisan primary, by petition, or by convention.

claim: City elections remain subject to the state's regular election dates notwithstanding any charter
quote: Notwithstanding another provision of this act or a charter provision, an election under this act is subject to section 641 of the Michigan election law

claim: No city charter may conflict with general state law
quote: No provision of any city charter shall conflict with or contravene the provisions of any general law of the state.

claim: Cities are created or enlarged only by a petition-started incorporation process, not automatically by population
quote: by proceedings originating by petition therefor signed by qualified electors who are freeholders

claim: Cities once incorporated under the fourth class city act have been home rule cities since 1980
quote: Effective January 1, 1980, a city incorporated under this act shall be deemed a home rule city

claim: Voters of each city and village may frame, adopt and amend a charter under general law
quote: Under general laws the electors of each city and village shall have the power and authority to frame, adopt and amend its charter

claim: General law village elections are nonpartisan regardless of charter or ordinance
quote: Notwithstanding a charter provision or ordinance to the contrary, village elections shall be nonpartisan.

claim: Home rule village elections are nonpartisan regardless of charter; a home rule village elects a president, clerk and legislative body
quote: Notwithstanding a charter provision to the contrary, a village election shall be nonpartisan.

claim: A general law village elects a president, six trustees, a clerk and a treasurer by default
quote: the following officers shall be elected: a president, 6 trustees, 1 clerk, and 1 treasurer

claim: A general law village council may by two-thirds vote cut trustees to four, change term lengths, or make the clerk or treasurer appointed
quote: may provide by ordinance for the reduction in the number of trustees to 4

claim: Village residents vote as electors of the township the village sits in; villages stay part of their township
quote: An individual who is a registered elector of the township in which the village is located and who is a resident of the village may vote at any election in the village.

claim: If a village charter does not set its election method, the village follows the township rules
quote: the village shall nominate and elect its officers in accordance with the provisions governing the selection of township officers

claim: A large city (1970 population over 150,000) may lengthen terms to four years by ordinance, subject to a referendum petition
quote: may provide by ordinance for a term of office of up to 4 years for mayor and other elected city officials

claim: An officer elected at the odd year general election for an odd number of years serves one year longer than the charter says
quote: shall, after September 1, 2004, be elected for a term of 1 year longer than provided by law or charter
